1: //! # Syntax Errors: Parser-Level and Semantic Syntax Validation
2: //!
3: //! This module implements syntax error checks that detect issues tree-sitter flags
4: //! as ERROR/MISSING nodes, as well as semantic syntax issues the parser cannot catch
5: //! (invalid operators, bad file names, structural violations).
6: //!
7: //! ## Check IDs
8: //!
9: //! | Check ID | Description                                              |
10: //! |----------|----------------------------------------------------------|
11: //! | SYNER    | ERROR node detected in parse tree                        |
12: //! | BDFIL    | File name doesn't follow MATLAB naming rules             |
13: //! | BADNE    | Source contains `!=` (MATLAB uses `~=`)                  |
14: //! | BADOT    | Source contains `..` not part of `...`                   |
15: //! | TWOCM    | Source contains `,,`                                     |
16: //! | CLIS     | class_definition in a script file                        |
17: //! | CLTWO    | Multiple class_definition nodes in one file              |
18: //! | SOFOC    | Statements outside a class_definition in a class file    |
19: //! | SEMFU    | File has only empty statements (only `;` and whitespace) |
20: //! | FNDOT    | Function name contains dots outside class methods block  |
21: //! | FNSWA    | Function name doesn't start with alphabetic character    |
22: //! | NOPAR    | ERROR node looks like a missing closing bracket          |
23: //! | ENDCT    | ERROR node suggesting missing END                        |
24: //! | EOFMI    | File ends with ERROR node (incomplete)                   |
25: //! | NOLHS    | Assignment with empty left side                          |
26: //! | BADCH    | Invalid control characters in source                     |
27: //! | BADSP    | Non-ASCII whitespace characters in source                |
28: //! | REDEF    | Same identifier used as both function name and variable  |
29: //! | SEPEXR   | Missing newline/semicolon between statements             |
30: //!
31: //! ## Configuration
32: //!
33: //! ```toml
34: //! [lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]
35: //! disabled_checks = []
36: //! ```
37:

39: use std::ops::Range;

42: use serde::Deserialize;

50: ///
51: /// Deserialized from the `[lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]` section in `.mlt.toml`.
52: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
53: pub struct SyntaxErrorsConfig {
54:     /// List of individual check IDs to disable (e.g., `["BADOT", "TWOCM"]`).
55:     #[serde(default)]

63: /// Syntax Errors Engine: a file-level rule that performs parser-level and
64: /// semantic syntax validation in a single pass.
65: pub struct SyntaxErrorsEngine {
66:     /// Set of disabled check IDs for fast lookup.
67:     disabled: HashSet<String>,
68: }

70: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
71:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
72:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
73:         let rule_config: SyntaxErrorsConfig = config.rule_params("SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE");
74:         let disabled: HashSet<String> = rule_config.disabled_checks.into_iter().collect();
75:         Box::new(Self { disabled })
76:     }

78:     /// Returns true if the given check ID is enabled.
79:     fn is_check_enabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
80:         !self.disabled.contains(check_id)
81:     }

84:     // Source text scanning (BADNE, BADOT, TWOCM, BADCH, BADSP)
85:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

87:     /// Collect byte ranges of all comment and string nodes to skip during
88:     /// source-level scanning.
89:     fn collect_skip_ranges(node: Node, ranges: &mut Vec<Range<usize>>) {
90:         if node.kind() == "comment" || node.kind() == "string" {
91:             ranges.push(node.byte_range());
92:             return;
93:         }
94:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
95:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
96:             Self::collect_skip_ranges(child, ranges);
97:         }
98:     }

100:     /// Check if a byte position is inside a skip range.
101:     fn in_skip_range(pos: usize, ranges: &[Range<usize>]) -> bool {
102:         ranges.iter().any(|r| r.contains(&pos))
103:     }
104: 
105:     /// Scan source text for BADNE (`!=`), BADOT (`..` not `...`), TWOCM (`,,`),
106:     /// BADCH (invalid control chars), and BADSP (non-ASCII whitespace).
107:     fn scan_source_text(
108:         &self,
109:         source: &str,
110:         skip_ranges: &[Range<usize>],
111:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
112:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
113:         let bytes = source.as_bytes();
114:         let len = bytes.len();
115: 
116:         // Track line/column for diagnostics.
117:         let mut line = 1usize;
118:         let mut line_start = 0usize;
119: 
120:         let mut i = 0;
121:         while i < len {
122:             let b = bytes[i];
123: 
124:             // Track newlines.
125:             if b == b'\n' {
126:                 line += 1;
127:                 line_start = i + 1;
128:                 i += 1;
129:                 continue;
130:             }
131: 
132:             // BADCH: Invalid control characters (< 0x20 except \t, \n, \r).
133:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADCH")
134:                 && b < 0x20
135:                 && b != b'\t'
136:                 && b != b'\n'
137:                 && b != b'\r'
138:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
139:             {
140:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
141:                     rule_id: "BADCH",
142:                     message: format!(
143:                         "Invalid control character (0x{:02X}) in source",
144:                         b
145:                     ),
146:                     severity: Severity::Error,
147:                     byte_range: i..i + 1,
148:                     line,
149:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
150:                     fix: None,
151:                 });
152:                 i += 1;
153:                 continue;
154:             }
155: 
156:             // BADSP: Non-ASCII whitespace detection.
157:             // Check for multi-byte UTF-8 sequences that are whitespace.
158:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADSP") && b > 0x7F && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges) {
159:                 // Decode the UTF-8 character at this position.
160:                 if let Some(ch) = source[i..].chars().next() {
161:                     if ch.is_whitespace() && ch != ' ' && ch != '\t' && ch != '\n' && ch != '\r' {
162:                         let ch_len = ch.len_utf8();
163:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
164:                             rule_id: "BADSP",
165:                             message: format!(
166:                                 "Non-ASCII whitespace character (U+{:04X}) in source",
167:                                 ch as u32
168:                             ),
169:                             severity: Severity::Error,
170:                             byte_range: i..i + ch_len,
171:                             line,
172:                             column: i - line_start + 1,
173:                             fix: None,
174:                         });
175:                         i += ch_len;
176:                         continue;
177:                     }
178:                 }
179:             }
180: 
181:             // BADNE: `!=` (MATLAB uses `~=`).
182:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADNE")
183:                 && b == b'!'
184:                 && i + 1 < len
185:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b'='
186:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
187:             {
188:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
189:                     rule_id: "BADNE",
190:                     message: "Use '~=' instead of '!=' for not-equal in MATLAB".to_string(),
191:                     severity: Severity::Error,
192:                     byte_range: i..i + 2,
193:                     line,
194:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
195:                     fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::new(i..i + 2, "~=")),
196:                 });
197:                 i += 2;
198:                 continue;
199:             }
200: 
201:             // BADOT: `..` not part of `...` (line continuation).
202:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADOT")
203:                 && b == b'.'
204:                 && i + 1 < len
205:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b'.'
206:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
207:             {
208:                 // Check if this is part of `...` (line continuation).
209:                 let is_ellipsis = i + 2 < len && bytes[i + 2] == b'.';
210:                 if !is_ellipsis {
211:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
212:                         rule_id: "BADOT",
213:                         message: "Invalid '..' operator; did you mean '...' (line continuation)?"
214:                             .to_string(),
215:                         severity: Severity::Error,
216:                         byte_range: i..i + 2,
217:                         line,
218:                         column: i - line_start + 1,
219:                         fix: None,
220:                     });
221:                     i += 2;
222:                     continue;
223:                 } else {
224:                     // Skip the whole `...`.
225:                     i += 3;
226:                     continue;
227:                 }
228:             }
229: 
230:             // TWOCM: `,,` (double comma).
231:             if self.is_check_enabled("TWOCM")
232:                 && b == b','
233:                 && i + 1 < len
234:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b','
235:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
236:             {
237:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
238:                     rule_id: "TWOCM",
239:                     message: "Double comma ',,'; possible typo".to_string(),
240:                     severity: Severity::Error,
241:                     byte_range: i..i + 2,
242:                     line,
243:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
244:                     fix: None,
245:                 });
246:                 i += 2;
247:                 continue;
248:             }
249: 
250:             // Advance past multi-byte UTF-8 characters.
251:             if b > 0x7F {
252:                 if let Some(ch) = source[i..].chars().next() {
253:                     i += ch.len_utf8();
254:                     continue;
255:                 }
256:             }
257: 
258:             i += 1;
259:         }

261:         diagnostics
262:     }

268:     /// Walk the tree and collect diagnostics for ERROR and MISSING nodes.
269:     fn check_error_nodes(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
270:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
271:         self.walk_error_nodes(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
272: 
273:         // EOFMI: Check if file ends with ERROR node.
274:         if self.is_check_enabled("EOFMI") {
275:             if let Some(last) = Self::last_descendant(root) {
276:                 if last.is_error() || last.is_missing() {
277:                     let start = last.start_byte();
278:                     let end = last.end_byte().max(start + 1);
279:                     let pos = last.start_position();
280:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
281:                         rule_id: "EOFMI",
282:                         message: "File ends with an incomplete or erroneous construct"
283:                             .to_string(),
284:                         severity: Severity::Error,
285:                         byte_range: start..end,
286:                         line: pos.row + 1,

297:     /// Recursive DFS to find ERROR/MISSING nodes and classify them.
298:     fn walk_error_nodes(
299:         &self,
300:         node: Node,
301:         source: &str,
302:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
303:     ) {
304:         if node.is_error() {
305:             let start = node.start_byte();
306:             let end = node.end_byte().max(start + 1);
307:             let pos = node.start_position();
308:             let text = &source[start..end.min(source.len())];

310:             // Classify the error node.
311:             // NOPAR: Looks like a missing closing bracket.
312:             if self.is_check_enabled("NOPAR") && Self::looks_like_missing_bracket(text) {
313:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
314:                     rule_id: "NOPAR",
315:                     message: "Possible missing closing bracket/parenthesis".to_string(),

317:                     byte_range: start..end,
318:                     line: pos.row + 1,
319:                     column: pos.column + 1,
320:                     fix: None,
321:                 });
322:             }
323:             // ENDCT: Looks like a missing END.
324:             else if self.is_check_enabled("ENDCT") && Self::looks_like_missing_end(text, &node) {
325:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
326:                     rule_id: "ENDCT",
327:                     message: "Possible missing 'end' keyword".to_string(),
328:                     severity: Severity::Error,
329:                     byte_range: start..end,
330:                     line: pos.row + 1,
331:                     column: pos.column + 1,
332:                     fix: None,
333:                 });
334:             }
335:             // SYNER: Generic syntax error.

340:                 } else {
341:                     format!("Syntax error near '{snippet}'")
342:                 };
343:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
344:                     rule_id: "SYNER",
345:                     message: msg,
346:                     severity: Severity::Error,
347:                     byte_range: start..end,
348:                     line: pos.row + 1,

350:                     fix: None,
351:                 });
352:             }
353:         } else if node.is_missing() && self.is_check_enabled("SYNER") {

355:             let end = node.end_byte().max(start + 1);

374:     /// Heuristic: does this error text look like an unclosed bracket?
375:     fn looks_like_missing_bracket(text: &str) -> bool {
376:         let opens: usize = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == '(' || c == '[' || c == '{').count();
377:         let closes: usize = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == ')' || c == ']' || c == '}').count();
378:         opens > closes
379:     }

381:     /// Heuristic: does this error look like a missing `end`?
382:     fn looks_like_missing_end(text: &str, node: &Node) -> bool {
383:         // If the error node is preceded by block-opening keywords.
384:         let block_openers = [
385:             "if", "for", "while", "switch", "try", "function", "classdef",
386:             "properties", "methods", "events", "enumeration",
387:         ];
388:         // Check text for block openers without matching end.
389:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
390:         let has_opener = block_openers.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));
391:         let has_end = lower.contains("end");
392: 
393:         if has_opener && !has_end {
394:             return true;
395:         }
396: 
397:         // Check if previous sibling is a block statement.
398:         if let Some(prev) = node.prev_sibling() {
399:             let kind = prev.kind();
400:             if block_openers.contains(&kind) {
401:                 return true;
402:             }
403:         }
404: 
405:         false
406:     }

412:     /// Validate file name against MATLAB naming rules.
413:     fn check_file_name(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {

416:         if !self.is_check_enabled("BDFIL") {
417:             return diagnostics;

420:         if let Some(stem) = ctx.file_path.file_stem() {

423:             let valid = !name.is_empty()
424:                 && name.len() <= 63
425:                 && name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
426:                 && name.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_');

435:                 } else {

461:         let mut has_any_real_content = false;
462: 
463:         for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
464:             let kind = child.kind();
465:             match kind {
466:                 "class_definition" => class_count += 1,
467:                 "function_definition" => {
468:                     has_function_def = true;
469:                     has_any_real_content = true;
470:                 }
471:                 "comment" => {} // Comments don't count as content.
472:                 "expression_statement" => {
473:                     // Check if it's just a semicolon.
474:                     let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
475:                     let trimmed = text.trim();
476:                     if trimmed == ";" {
477:                         // Empty statement — doesn't count as real content.
478:                     } else {
479:                         has_non_class_statements = true;
480:                         has_any_real_content = true;
481:                     }
482:                 }
483:                 _ if !child.is_error() && kind != "\n" => {
484:                     has_non_class_statements = true;
485:                     has_any_real_content = true;
486:                 }
487:                 _ => {}
488:             }
489:         }
490: 
491:         // CLTWO: Multiple class definitions in one file.
492:         if self.is_check_enabled("CLTWO") && class_count > 1 {
493:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
494:                 rule_id: "CLTWO",
495:                 message: format!(
496:                     "File contains {class_count} class definitions; only one is allowed per file"
497:                 ),
498:                 severity: Severity::Error,
499:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
500:                 line: 1,
501:                 column: 1,
502:                 fix: None,
503:             });
504:         }
505: 
506:         // CLIS: Class definition in a script file (non-function statements exist).
507:         if self.is_check_enabled("CLIS")
508:             && class_count > 0
509:             && has_non_class_statements
510:             && !has_function_def
511:         {
512:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
513:                 rule_id: "CLIS",
514:                 message: "Class definition in a script file; statements exist outside the class"
515:                     .to_string(),
516:                 severity: Severity::Error,
517:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
518:                 line: 1,
519:                 column: 1,
520:                 fix: None,
521:             });
522:         }
523: 
524:         // SOFOC: Statements outside a class definition in a class file.
525:         if self.is_check_enabled("SOFOC")
526:             && class_count > 0
527:             && has_non_class_statements
528:             && has_function_def
529:         {
530:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
531:                 rule_id: "SOFOC",
532:                 message:
533:                     "Statements outside class definition in a class file are not allowed"
534:                         .to_string(),
535:                 severity: Severity::Error,
536:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
537:                 line: 1,
538:                 column: 1,
539:                 fix: None,
540:             });
541:         }
542: 
543:         // SEMFU: File has only empty statements (only `;` and whitespace).
544:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEMFU")
545:             && !has_any_real_content
546:             && class_count == 0
547:             && !source.trim().is_empty()
548:         {
549:             // Verify the file truly only has semicolons, whitespace, and comments.
550:             let only_empty = source
551:                 .lines()
552:                 .all(|line| {
553:                     let trimmed = line.trim();
554:                     trimmed.is_empty()
555:                         || trimmed == ";"
556:                         || trimmed.starts_with('%')
557:                 });
558:             if only_empty {
559:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
560:                     rule_id: "SEMFU",
561:                     message: "File contains only empty statements (semicolons and whitespace)"
562:                         .to_string(),
563:                     severity: Severity::Error,
564:                     byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
565:                     line: 1,
566:                     column: 1,
567:                     fix: None,
568:                 });
569:             }
570:         }
571: 
572:         diagnostics
573:     }

579:     /// Check function names for issues (FNDOT, FNSWA).
580:     fn check_function_names(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
581:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
582:         self.walk_function_names(root, source, &mut diagnostics, false);
583:         diagnostics

586:     /// Recursively walk to find function_definition nodes and validate names.
587:     fn walk_function_names(
588:         &self,
589:         node: Node,
590:         source: &str,
591:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
592:         in_methods_block: bool,
593:     ) {
594:         let kind = node.kind();
595:         let is_methods = kind == "methods";
596: 
597:         if kind == "function_definition" {
598:             // Find the function name node.
599:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
600:                 let name = &source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()];
601:                 let pos = name_node.start_position();
602: 
603:                 // FNSWA: Function name doesn't start with alphabetic character.
604:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNSWA")
605:                     && !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
606:                 {
607:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
608:                         rule_id: "FNSWA",
609:                         message: format!(
610:                             "Function name '{}' must start with an alphabetic character",
611:                             name
612:                         ),
613:                         severity: Severity::Error,
614:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
615:                         line: pos.row + 1,
616:                         column: pos.column + 1,
617:                         fix: None,
618:                     });
619:                 }
620: 
621:                 // FNDOT: Function name contains dots but is not in a class methods block.
622:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNDOT") && name.contains('.') && !in_methods_block {
623:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
624:                         rule_id: "FNDOT",
625:                         message: format!(
626:                             "Function name '{}' contains dots but is not in a class methods block",
627:                             name
628:                         ),
629:                         severity: Severity::Error,
630:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
631:                         line: pos.row + 1,
632:                         column: pos.column + 1,
633:                         fix: None,
634:                     });
635:                 }
636:             }
637:         }
638: 
639:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
640:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
641:             self.walk_function_names(
642:                 child,
643:                 source,
644:                 diagnostics,
645:                 in_methods_block || is_methods,
646:             );
647:         }
648:     }

651:     // Statement validation (NOLHS, SEPEXR, REDEF)

654:     /// Check statements for issues (NOLHS, SEPEXR, REDEF).
655:     fn check_statements(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
656:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
657: 
658:         // Collect function names and variable assignments for REDEF.
659:         let mut function_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
660:         let mut variable_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
661:         let mut redef_reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
662: 
663:         self.walk_statements(
664:             root,
665:             source,
666:             &mut diagnostics,
667:             &mut function_names,
668:             &mut variable_names,
669:             &mut redef_reported,
670:         );
671: 
672:         diagnostics
673:     }

675:     /// Recursively walk statements for validation.
676:     fn walk_statements(
677:         &self,
678:         node: Node,
679:         source: &str,
680:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
681:         function_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
682:         variable_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
683:         redef_reported: &mut HashSet<String>,
684:     ) {
685:         let kind = node.kind();
686: 
687:         // NOLHS: Assignment with empty left side.
688:         if self.is_check_enabled("NOLHS") && kind == "assignment" {
689:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
690:                 let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
691:                 if lhs_text.trim().is_empty() {
692:                     let pos = node.start_position();
693:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
694:                         rule_id: "NOLHS",
695:                         message: "Assignment with empty left-hand side".to_string(),
696:                         severity: Severity::Error,
697:                         byte_range: node.byte_range(),
698:                         line: pos.row + 1,
699:                         column: pos.column + 1,
700:                         fix: None,
701:                     });
702:                 }
703:             }
704:         }
705: 
706:         // REDEF: Track function definitions and variable assignments.
707:         if kind == "function_definition" {
708:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
709:                 let name = source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()].to_string();
710:                 if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
711:                     && variable_names.contains(&name)
712:                     && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
713:                 {
714:                     let pos = name_node.start_position();
715:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
716:                         rule_id: "REDEF",
717:                         message: format!(
718:                             "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
719:                             name
720:                         ),
721:                         severity: Severity::Error,
722:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
723:                         line: pos.row + 1,
724:                         column: pos.column + 1,
725:                         fix: None,
726:                     });
727:                     redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
728:                 }
729:                 function_names.insert(name);
730:             }
731:         }
732: 
733:         if kind == "assignment" {
734:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
735:                 let lhs_kind = lhs.kind();
736:                 if lhs_kind == "identifier" {
737:                     let name = source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()].to_string();
738:                     if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
739:                         && function_names.contains(&name)
740:                         && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
741:                     {
742:                         let pos = lhs.start_position();
743:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
744:                             rule_id: "REDEF",
745:                             message: format!(
746:                                 "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
747:                                 name
748:                             ),
749:                             severity: Severity::Error,
750:                             byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
751:                             line: pos.row + 1,
752:                             column: pos.column + 1,
753:                             fix: None,
754:                         });
755:                         redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
756:                     }
757:                     variable_names.insert(name);
758:                 }
759:             }
760:         }
761: 
762:         // SEPEXR: Missing separator between statements.
763:         // Check consecutive children of block/source_file that are statements
764:         // on the same line without separator.
765:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEPEXR") && (kind == "source_file" || kind == "block") {
766:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
767:             let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
768: 
769:             for pair in children.windows(2) {
770:                 let prev = pair[0];
771:                 let curr = pair[1];
772: 
773:                 // Skip error nodes and comments.
774:                 if prev.is_error() || curr.is_error() {
775:                     continue;
776:                 }
777:                 if prev.kind() == "comment" || curr.kind() == "comment" {
778:                     continue;
779:                 }
780: 
781:                 // Check if they're on the same line with no separator.
782:                 let prev_end = prev.end_position();
783:                 let curr_start = curr.start_position();
784: 
785:                 if prev_end.row == curr_start.row {
786:                     // Check the text between them for a separator (; or ,).
787:                     let between_start = prev.end_byte();
788:                     let between_end = curr.start_byte();
789:                     if between_start < between_end {
790:                         let between = &source[between_start..between_end];
791:                         let has_separator =
792:                             between.contains(';') || between.contains(',');
793:                         if !has_separator {
794:                             let pos = curr.start_position();
795:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
796:                                 rule_id: "SEPEXR",
797:                                 message:
798:                                     "Missing semicolon or newline between statements"
799:                                         .to_string(),
800:                                 severity: Severity::Error,
801:                                 byte_range: curr.byte_range(),
802:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
803:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
804:                                 fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::insert(between_start, ";")),
805:                             });
806:                         }
807:                     }
808:                 }
809:             }
810:         }
811: 
812:         // Recurse into children.
813:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
814:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
815:             self.walk_statements(
816:                 child,
817:                 source,
818:                 diagnostics,
819:                 function_names,
820:                 variable_names,
821:                 redef_reported,
822:             );
823:         }
824:     }

830:     /// Find the last (rightmost, deepest) descendant node in a tree.
831:     fn last_descendant(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
832:         let child_count = node.child_count();
833:         if child_count == 0 {
834:             return Some(node);
835:         }
836:         let last_child = node.child(child_count - 1)?;
837:         Self::last_descendant(last_child)
838:     }
839: }

1: # NOSEMI - Trailing Semicolon Missing
2: 
3: **Default severity:** Info
4: **Auto-fix:** Yes
5: **Category:** Formatting
6: **Can be disabled:** Yes
7: 
8: ## What this rule does
9: 
10: Flags MATLAB statements that do not end with a trailing semicolon (`;`). This applies to statements that produce a value — primarily assignments, function calls, and commands at the statement level.
11: 
12: ## Why this matters
13: 
14: - **Performance**: In loops, unsuppressed output causes significant slowdowns due to console I/O on every iteration
15: - **Noise**: Unintended console output clutters the Command Window, making it harder to find real output
16: - **Intent**: Without a semicolon, it's ambiguous whether the output was intentional (for debugging) or accidental
17: - **CI/CD**: Stray output in automated MATLAB scripts can pollute logs or interfere with output parsing
18: 
19: ## Examples
20: 
21: ### Correct
22: 
23: ```matlab
24: x = compute_value();
25: data = load('file.mat');
26: result = process(data);
27: 
28: % Intentional output (configure ignore_functions)
29: disp('Processing complete');
30: fprintf('Result: %d\n', result);
31: ```
32: 
33: ### Incorrect
34: 
35: ```matlab
36: x = compute_value()
37: data = load('file.mat')
38: result = process(data)
39: ```
40: 
41: ### Fixed
42: 
43: ```matlab
44: x = compute_value();
45: data = load('file.mat');
46: result = process(data);
47: ```
48: 
49: ## Configuration
50: 
51: ```toml title=".mlt.toml"
52: [lint.rules.NOSEMI]
53: severity = "info"
54: ignore_functions = ["disp", "fprintf", "warning", "error"]
55: ```
56: 
57: ### Parameters
58: 
59: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
60: | --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
61: | `severity` | string | `"info"` | Severity level (`"error"`, `"warn"`, `"info"`, `"off"`) |
62: | `ignore_functions` | array of strings | `[]` | Function names to exclude from this check |
63: 
64: ### `ignore_functions`
65: 
66: A list of function names that are commonly used for intentional console output. When a `function_call` or `command` statement calls one of these functions, the rule will not flag it even without a semicolon.
67: 
68: Common values:
69: 
70: ```toml
71: ignore_functions = [
72:     "disp",
73:     "fprintf",
74:     "warning",
75:     "error",
76:     "assert",
77:     "sprintf",  # usually assigned, but sometimes standalone
78: ]
79: ```
80: 
81: ## Automatic fixes
82: 
83: This rule inserts a semicolon (`;`) immediately after the end of the statement:
84: 
85: ```diff
86: - x = compute_value()
87: + x = compute_value();
88: ```
89: 
90: The fix is always safe — it suppresses output but does not change program behavior.
91: 
92: ## Target node types
93: 
94: This rule triggers on the following tree-sitter node types when they appear at statement level (direct children of `source_file` or `block`):
95: 
96: - `assignment` — Variable assignments (`a = expr`)
97: - `function_call` — Function calls used as statements (`foo(x)`)
98: - `command` — Command-syntax calls (`cd dir`, `help topic`)
99: 
100: Sub-expressions (e.g., `bar(1)` inside `x = foo(bar(1))`) are **not** flagged.
101: 
102: ## Related rules

105: - `NO4LP` — Missing indentation for loop body

64:

66: 
67: Critical issues that likely indicate bugs or broken code:
68:

71: - Syntax errors

112: performance = "off"           # Disable all performance rules
113: compatibility = "warn"        # Override all compatibility rules to warning

142: mlt --fix src/**/*.m

1: # UNSET - Invalid Operator on Left Side of Assignment
2: 
3: **Default severity:** Error
4: **Auto-fix:** No
5: **Category:** Syntax Errors
6: **Can be disabled:** Yes
7: 
8: ## What this rule does
9: 
10: Flags assignments where the left side of `=` is an operator expression, such as a comparison, arithmetic operation, logical operation, or unary operator. MATLAB requires the left side of an assignment to be a valid target (a variable, indexed element, field, or output list):
11: 
12: ```matlab
13: x == 5 = 3;    % comparison_operator on the LHS
14: x + 1 = 2;     % binary_operator on the LHS
15: ```
16: 
17: This is a sub-check of the `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE` rule. It triggers on `assignment` nodes whose left side is an operator, and on `ERROR` nodes that follow a statement-level operator expression and begin with `=` (which is how the parser represents `x == 5 = 3;` and `x + 1 = 2;`).
18: 
19: ## Why this matters
20: 
21: - **Broken code**: `x == 5 = 3` is not valid MATLAB and fails to run — the error is emitted at parse time
22: - **Diagnosis**: The Code Analyzer message ("Invalid use of operator on the left side of an assignment") is clearer than a generic syntax error, pointing directly at the offending operator expression
23: - **Typo detection**: `x == x + 1` is a common typo for `x = x + 1`; a `+` or `==` on the left of `=` almost always indicates a missing variable name
24: 
25: ## Examples
26: 
27: ### Correct
28: 
29: ```matlab
30: x = 5;
31: y = x == 5;      % operator on the right side is fine
32: x(1) = 5;        % indexed assignment is valid
33: obj.field = 5;   % field assignment is valid
34: [a, b] = f();    % multi-output list is valid
35: ```
36: 
37: ### Incorrect
38: 
39: ```matlab
40: x == 5 = 3;   % comparison operator on the left
41: x + 1 = 2;    % binary operator on the left
42: -x = 3;       % unary operator on the left
43: x' = 3;       % transpose operator on the left
44: ```
45: 
46: ## Configuration
47: 
48: As a sub-check of the `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE`, disable it via the engine's `disabled_checks` list:
49: 
50: ```toml title=".mlt.toml"
51: [lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]
52: severity = "error"
53: disabled_checks = ["UNSET"]
54: ```
55: 
56: ### Parameters
57: 
58: | Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
59: | --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
60: | `severity` | string | `"error"` | Severity level (`"error"`, `"warn"`, `"info"`, `"off"`) |
61: | `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Sub-check IDs to disable within `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE` (add `"UNSET"` to disable this check) |
62:

562:         // SEMFU: File has only empty statements (only `;` and whitespace).
563:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEMFU")
564:             && !has_any_real_content
565:             && class_count == 0
566:             && !source.trim().is_empty()
567:         {
568:             // Verify the file truly only has semicolons, whitespace, and comments.
569:             let only_empty = source
570:                 .lines()
571:                 .all(|line| {
572:                     let trimmed = line.trim();
573:                     trimmed.is_empty()
574:                         || trimmed == ";"
575:                         || trimmed.starts_with('%')
576:                 });
577:             if only_empty {
578:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
579:                     rule_id: "SEMFU",
580:                     message: "File contains only empty statements (semicolons and whitespace)"
581:                         .to_string(),
582:                     severity: Severity::Error,
583:                     byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
584:                     line: 1,
585:                     column: 1,
586:                     fix: None,
587:                 });
588:             }
589:         }
590: 
591:         diagnostics
592:     }

598:     /// Check function names for issues (FNDOT, FNSWA).
599:     fn check_function_names(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {

605:     /// Recursively walk to find function_definition nodes and validate names.
606:     fn walk_function_names(
607:         &self,
608:         node: Node,
609:         source: &str,
610:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
611:         in_methods_block: bool,
612:     ) {
613:         let kind = node.kind();
614:         let is_methods = kind == "methods";
615: 
616:         if kind == "function_definition" {
617:             // Find the function name node.
618:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
619:                 let name = &source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()];
620:                 let pos = name_node.start_position();
621: 
622:                 // FNSWA: Function name doesn't start with alphabetic character.
623:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNSWA")
624:                     && !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
625:                 {
626:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
627:                         rule_id: "FNSWA",
628:                         message: format!(
629:                             "Function name '{}' must start with an alphabetic character",
630:                             name
631:                         ),
632:                         severity: Severity::Error,
633:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
634:                         line: pos.row + 1,
635:                         column: pos.column + 1,
636:                         fix: None,
637:                     });
638:                 }
639: 
640:                 // FNDOT: Function name contains dots but is not in a class methods block.
641:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNDOT") && name.contains('.') && !in_methods_block {
642:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
643:                         rule_id: "FNDOT",
644:                         message: format!(
645:                             "Function name '{}' contains dots but is not in a class methods block",
646:                             name
647:                         ),
648:                         severity: Severity::Error,
649:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
650:                         line: pos.row + 1,
651:                         column: pos.column + 1,
652:                         fix: None,
653:                     });
654:                 }
655:             }
656:         }
657: 
658:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
659:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
660:             self.walk_function_names(
661:                 child,
662:                 source,
663:                 diagnostics,
664:                 in_methods_block || is_methods,
665:             );
666:         }
667:     }

673:     /// Check statements for issues (NOLHS, SEPEXR, REDEF).
674:     fn check_statements(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
675:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
676: 
677:         // Collect function names and variable assignments for REDEF.
678:         let mut function_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
679:         let mut variable_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
680:         let mut redef_reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
681: 
682:         self.walk_statements(
683:             root,
684:             source,
685:             &mut diagnostics,
686:             &mut function_names,
687:             &mut variable_names,
688:             &mut redef_reported,
689:         );
690: 
691:         diagnostics
692:     }
693: 
694:     /// Recursively walk statements for validation.
695:     fn walk_statements(
696:         &self,
697:         node: Node,
698:         source: &str,
699:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
700:         function_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
701:         variable_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
702:         redef_reported: &mut HashSet<String>,
703:     ) {
704:         let kind = node.kind();
705: 
706:         // NOLHS: Assignment with empty left side.
707:         if self.is_check_enabled("NOLHS") && kind == "assignment" {
708:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
709:                 let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
710:                 if lhs_text.trim().is_empty() {
711:                     let pos = node.start_position();
712:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
713:                         rule_id: "NOLHS",
714:                         message: "Assignment with empty left-hand side".to_string(),
715:                         severity: Severity::Error,
716:                         byte_range: node.byte_range(),
717:                         line: pos.row + 1,
718:                         column: pos.column + 1,
719:                         fix: None,
720:                     });
721:                 }
722:             }
723:         }
724: 
725:         // REDEF: Track function definitions and variable assignments.
726:         if kind == "function_definition" {
727:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
728:                 let name = source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()].to_string();
729:                 if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
730:                     && variable_names.contains(&name)
731:                     && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
732:                 {
733:                     let pos = name_node.start_position();
734:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
735:                         rule_id: "REDEF",
736:                         message: format!(
737:                             "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
738:                             name
739:                         ),
740:                         severity: Severity::Error,
741:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
742:                         line: pos.row + 1,
743:                         column: pos.column + 1,
744:                         fix: None,
745:                     });
746:                     redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
747:                 }
748:                 function_names.insert(name);
749:             }
750:         }
751: 
752:         if kind == "assignment" {
753:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
754:                 let lhs_kind = lhs.kind();
755:                 if lhs_kind == "identifier" {
756:                     let name = source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()].to_string();
757:                     if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
758:                         && function_names.contains(&name)
759:                         && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
760:                     {
761:                         let pos = lhs.start_position();
762:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
763:                             rule_id: "REDEF",
764:                             message: format!(
765:                                 "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
766:                                 name
767:                             ),
768:                             severity: Severity::Error,
769:                             byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
770:                             line: pos.row + 1,
771:                             column: pos.column + 1,
772:                             fix: None,
773:                         });
774:                         redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
775:                     }
776:                     variable_names.insert(name);
777:                 }
778:             }
779:         }
780: 
781:         // SEPEXR: Missing separator between statements.
782:         // Check consecutive children of block/source_file that are statements
783:         // on the same line without separator.
784:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEPEXR") && (kind == "source_file" || kind == "block") {
785:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
786:             let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
787: 
788:             for pair in children.windows(2) {
789:                 let prev = pair[0];
790:                 let curr = pair[1];
791: 
792:                 // Skip error nodes and comments.
793:                 if prev.is_error() || curr.is_error() {
794:                     continue;
795:                 }
796:                 if prev.kind() == "comment" || curr.kind() == "comment" {
797:                     continue;
798:                 }
799: 
800:                 // Check if they're on the same line with no separator.
801:                 let prev_end = prev.end_position();
802:                 let curr_start = curr.start_position();
803: 
804:                 if prev_end.row == curr_start.row {
805:                     // Check the text between them for a separator (; or ,).
806:                     let between_start = prev.end_byte();
807:                     let between_end = curr.start_byte();
808:                     if between_start < between_end {
809:                         let between = &source[between_start..between_end];
810:                         let has_separator =
811:                             between.contains(';') || between.contains(',');
812:                         if !has_separator {
813:                             let pos = curr.start_position();
814:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
815:                                 rule_id: "SEPEXR",
816:                                 message:
817:                                     "Missing semicolon or newline between statements"
818:                                         .to_string(),
819:                                 severity: Severity::Error,
820:                                 byte_range: curr.byte_range(),
821:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
822:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
823:                                 fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::insert(between_start, ";")),
824:                             });
825:                         }
826:                     }
827:                 }
828:             }
829:         }
830: 
831:         // Recurse into children.
832:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
833:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
834:             self.walk_statements(
835:                 child,
836:                 source,
837:                 diagnostics,
838:                 function_names,
839:                 variable_names,
840:                 redef_reported,
841:             );
842:         }
843:     }

849:     /// Check assignment left-hand sides for invalid operator targets (UNSET)
850:     /// and multi-row output lists (LHROW).
851:     fn check_assignment_lhs(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
852:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
853:         self.walk_assignment_lhs(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
854:         diagnostics
855:     }

857:     /// Recursively walk assignment nodes and ERROR nodes to validate LHS.
858:     fn walk_assignment_lhs(&self, node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
859:         const OPERATOR_LHS_KINDS: [&str; 5] = [
860:             "comparison_operator",
861:             "binary_operator",
862:             "boolean_operator",
863:             "unary_operator",
864:             "postfix_operator",
865:         ];
866: 
867:         let kind = node.kind();
868: 
869:         if kind == "assignment" {
870:             let lhs = node.child_by_field_name("left");
871:             if let Some(lhs) = lhs {
872:                 let pos = lhs.start_position();
873: 
874:                 // UNSET: operator expression on the left side of `=`.
875:                 if self.is_check_enabled("UNSET") && OPERATOR_LHS_KINDS.contains(&lhs.kind()) {
876:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
877:                         rule_id: "UNSET",
878:                         message:
879:                             "Invalid use of operator on the left side of an assignment"
880:                                 .to_string(),
881:                         severity: Severity::Error,
882:                         byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
883:                         line: pos.row + 1,
884:                         column: pos.column + 1,
885:                         fix: None,
886:                     });
887:                 }
888: 
889:                 // LHROW: multi-output LHS containing a row separator (`;`).
890:                 if self.is_check_enabled("LHROW") && lhs.kind() == "multioutput_variable" {
891:                     let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
892:                     if lhs_text.contains(';') {
893:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
894:                             rule_id: "LHROW",
895:                             message: "The left side of an assignment cannot have multiple rows (';')"
896:                                 .to_string(),
897:                             severity: Severity::Error,
898:                             byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
899:                             line: pos.row + 1,
900:                             column: pos.column + 1,
901:                             fix: None,
902:                         });
903:                     }
904:                 }
905:             }
906:         }
907: 
908:         // UNSET fallback: the parser may emit an ERROR node (text starting
909:         // with `=`) as the sibling of a statement-level operator expression
910:         // instead of an assignment node (e.g., `x == 5 = 3;`).
911:         if self.is_check_enabled("UNSET") && node.is_error() {
912:             if let Some(prev) = node.prev_sibling() {
913:                 if OPERATOR_LHS_KINDS.contains(&prev.kind()) {
914:                     let err_text = &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()];
915:                     if err_text.trim_start().starts_with('=') {
916:                         let pos = prev.start_position();
917:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
918:                             rule_id: "UNSET",
919:                             message: "Invalid use of operator on the left side of an assignment"
920:                                 .to_string(),
921:                             severity: Severity::Error,
922:                             byte_range: prev.byte_range(),
923:                             line: pos.row + 1,
924:                             column: pos.column + 1,
925:                             fix: None,
926:                         });
927:                     }
928:                 }
929:             }
930:         }
931: 
932:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
933:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
934:             self.walk_assignment_lhs(child, source, diagnostics);
935:         }
936:     }

938:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
939:     // Reserved words and invalid ~ usage (RESWD, SYNEND, MCPLD, BADNOT,
940:     // BADNOTLHS)
941:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
942: 
943:     /// Check for reserved words used as identifiers (RESWD), invalid `end`
944:     /// usage (SYNEND), invalid property syntax (MCPLD), and invalid `~` usage
945:     /// (BADNOT, BADNOTLHS).
946:     fn check_reserved_and_not(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
947:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
948:         self.walk_reserved_and_not(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
949:         diagnostics
950:     }
951: 
952:     /// Recursively walk the tree for reserved-word and `~` misuse.
953:     fn walk_reserved_and_not(
954:         &self,
955:         node: Node,
956:         source: &str,
957:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
958:     ) {
959:         let kind = node.kind();
960: 
961:         if node.is_error() {
962:             let start = node.start_byte();
963:             let end = node.end_byte().max(start + 1);
964:             let pos = node.start_position();
965:             let text = &source[start..end.min(source.len())];
966: 
967:             // MCPLD: ERROR inside a property declaration in a properties block.
968:             if self.is_check_enabled("MCPLD") && Self::inside_property(node) {
969:                 let name = Self::ancestor_of_kind(node, "property")
970:                     .and_then(|prop| Self::first_child_text(prop, "identifier", source))
971:                     .unwrap_or("(unknown)");
972:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
973:                     rule_id: "MCPLD",
974:                     message: format!("Invalid property syntax at {name}"),
975:                     severity: Severity::Error,
976:                     byte_range: start..end,
977:                     line: pos.row + 1,
978:                     column: pos.column + 1,
979:                     fix: None,
980:                 });
981:             }
982: 
983:             // SYNEND takes priority over RESWD for `end`.
984:             if self.is_check_enabled("SYNEND") && Self::has_descendant_kind(node, "end_keyword")
985:             {
986:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
987:                     rule_id: "SYNEND",
988:                     message: "Invalid use for END operator".to_string(),
989:                     severity: Severity::Error,
990:                     byte_range: start..end,
991:                     line: pos.row + 1,
992:                     column: pos.column + 1,
993:                     fix: None,
994:                 });
995:             } else if self.is_check_enabled("RESWD") {
996:                 if let Some(kw) = Self::contains_reserved_word(text) {
997:                     if kw != "end" {
998:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
999:                             rule_id: "RESWD",
1000:                             message: "Invalid use of a reserved word.".to_string(),
1001:                             severity: Severity::Error,
1002:                             byte_range: start..end,
1003:                             line: pos.row + 1,
1004:                             column: pos.column + 1,
1005:                             fix: None,
1006:                         });
1007:                     }
1008:                 }
1009:             }
1010: 
1011:             // BADNOT: bare `~` statement.
1012:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADNOT") && text.trim() == "~" {
1013:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1014:                     rule_id: "BADNOT",
1015:                     message: "Using ~ to ignore a value is not permitted in this context."
1016:                         .to_string(),
1017:                     severity: Severity::Error,
1018:                     byte_range: start..end,
1019:                     line: pos.row + 1,
1020:                     column: pos.column + 1,
1021:                     fix: None,
1022:                 });
1023:             }
1024:         }
1025: 
1026:         // BADNOT: `~` used as a value operator with a malformed operand.
1027:         if kind == "not_operator"
1028:             && self.is_check_enabled("BADNOT")
1029:             && Self::has_error_or_missing_descendant(node)
1030:         {
1031:             let start = node.start_byte();
1032:             let end = node.end_byte();
1033:             let pos = node.start_position();
1034:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1035:                 rule_id: "BADNOT",
1036:                 message: "Using ~ to ignore a value is not permitted in this context."
1037:                     .to_string(),
1038:                 severity: Severity::Error,
1039:                 byte_range: start..end,
1040:                 line: pos.row + 1,
1041:                 column: pos.column + 1,
1042:                 fix: None,
1043:             });
1044:         }
1045: 
1046:         // BADNOTLHS: `~` adjacent to an output variable without a comma.
1047:         if kind == "multioutput_variable" && self.is_check_enabled("BADNOTLHS") {
1048:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
1049:             let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
1050:             for (i, child) in children.iter().enumerate() {
1051:                 if child.kind() != "ignored_argument" {
1052:                     continue;
1053:                 }
1054:                 let prev_is_id = i > 0 && children[i - 1].kind() == "identifier";
1055:                 let next_is_id = i + 1 < children.len() && children[i + 1].kind() == "identifier";
1056:                 if prev_is_id || next_is_id {
1057:                     let pos = child.start_position();
1058:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1059:                         rule_id: "BADNOTLHS",
1060:                         message: "Invalid use of logical not operator (~) on left side of an assignment. To use ~ to ignore function outputs, separate output variables with commas."
1061:                             .to_string(),
1062:                         severity: Severity::Error,
1063:                         byte_range: child.byte_range(),
1064:                         line: pos.row + 1,
1065:                         column: pos.column + 1,
1066:                         fix: None,
1067:                     });
1068:                 }
1069:             }
1070:         }
1071: 
1072:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
1073:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1074:             self.walk_reserved_and_not(child, source, diagnostics);
1075:         }
1076:     }

1078:     /// Returns the first reserved keyword appearing as a whole word in `text`.
1079:     fn contains_reserved_word(text: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
1080:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
1081:         RESERVED_KEYWORDS
1082:             .iter()
1083:             .find(|&&kw| Self::contains_whole_word(&lower, kw))
1084:             .copied()
1085:     }
1086: 
1087:     /// Whole-word substring check: `needle` must not be part of a larger word.
1088:     fn contains_whole_word(haystack: &str, needle: &str) -> bool {
1089:         let mut search_start = 0;
1090:         while let Some(rel) = haystack[search_start..].find(needle) {
1091:             let idx = search_start + rel;
1092:             let prev = haystack[..idx].chars().next_back();
1093:             let next = haystack[idx + needle.len()..].chars().next();
1094:             let left_ok = prev.is_none_or(|c| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() && c != '_');
1095:             let right_ok = next.is_none_or(|c| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() && c != '_');
1096:             if left_ok && right_ok {
1097:                 return true;
1098:             }
1099:             search_start = idx + needle.len();
1100:         }
1101:         false
1102:     }

1104:     /// Returns true if `node` or any of its descendants has the given kind.
1105:     fn has_descendant_kind(node: Node, kind: &str) -> bool {
1106:         if node.kind() == kind {
1107:             return true;
1108:         }
1109:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
1110:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1111:             if Self::has_descendant_kind(child, kind) {
1112:                 return true;
1113:             }
1114:         }
1115:         false
1116:     }
1117: 
1118:     /// Returns true if the node's subtree contains an ERROR or MISSING node.
1119:     fn has_error_or_missing_descendant(node: Node) -> bool {
1120:         if node.is_error() || node.is_missing() {
1121:             return true;
1122:         }
1123:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
1124:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1125:             if Self::has_error_or_missing_descendant(child) {
1126:                 return true;
1127:             }
1128:         }
1129:         false
1130:     }
1131: 
1132:     /// Returns true if `node` is a descendant of a `property` node inside a
1133:     /// `properties` block.
1134:     fn inside_property(node: Node) -> bool {
1135:         let mut current = node.parent();
1136:         while let Some(n) = current {
1137:             match n.kind() {
1138:                 "property" => return true,
1139:                 "properties" => return false,
1140:                 _ => {}
1141:             }
1142:             current = n.parent();
1143:         }
1144:         false
1145:     }

1147:     /// Returns the nearest ancestor of `node` with the given kind.
1148:     fn ancestor_of_kind<'tree>(node: Node<'tree>, kind: &str) -> Option<Node<'tree>> {
1149:         let mut current = node.parent();
1150:         while let Some(n) = current {
1151:             if n.kind() == kind {
1152:                 return Some(n);
1153:             }
1154:             current = n.parent();
1155:         }
1156:         None
1157:     }
1158: 
1159:     /// Returns the text of the first child of `node` with the given kind.
1160:     fn first_child_text<'tree>(
1161:         node: Node<'tree>,
1162:         kind: &str,
1163:         source: &'tree str,
1164:     ) -> Option<&'tree str> {
1165:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
1166:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1167:             if child.kind() == kind {
1168:                 return Some(&source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()]);
1169:             }
1170:         }
1171:         None
1172:     }

# ENDCT2 - An END Might Be Missing After a Block-Opening Keyword

**Default severity:** Error
**Auto-fix:** No
**Category:** Syntax Errors
**Can be disabled:** Yes

## What this rule does

Flags an unterminated block: a block-opening keyword (`if`, `for`, `while`, `switch`, `try`, `function`, `classdef`, `properties`, `methods`, `events`, or `enumeration`) appears without a matching `end`. This is a sub-check of the `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE` rule.

The check triggers on `ERROR` nodes produced by the parser when a block opener is not closed with `end`. The opener can appear in the error text itself (the common case — the parser wraps the whole unterminated construct in an `ERROR` node) or in the error's previous sibling.

```matlab
if x > 0
    y = 1;       % missing end for the if block
```

## Why this matters

- **Broken code**: Every block in MATLAB must be closed with `end`; an unterminated block fails to parse and the file does not run
- **Hidden damage**: A missing `end` often swallows subsequent code into the block, so errors appear far from the actual problem
- **Diagnosis**: The message ("An END might be missing...") points directly at the unterminated construct instead of a generic syntax error

## Examples

### Correct

```matlab
if x > 0
    y = 1;
end

for i = 1:10
    disp(i);
end

while x
    y = 1;
end
```

### Incorrect

```matlab
if x > 0
    y = 1;        % ENDCT2 fires here

for i = 1:10
    disp(i);      % ENDCT2 fires here

switch x
    case 1
        y = 1;    % ENDCT2 fires here
```

## Configuration

As a sub-check of the `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE`, disable it via the engine's `disabled_checks` list:

```toml title=".mlt.toml"
[lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]
severity = "error"
disabled_checks = ["ENDCT2"]
```

When a variant such as `ENDCT2` is disabled, the engine falls back to the generic `ENDCT` check so the missing-END condition is still reported. Disabling `ENDCT` itself suppresses all ENDCT family checks (`ENDCT`, `ENDCT2`, `ENDCT3`, `ENDCT4`).

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --------- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `severity` | string | `"error"` | Severity level (`"error"`, `"warn"`, `"info"`, `"off"`) |
| `disabled_checks` | array of strings | `[]` | Sub-check IDs to disable within `SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE` (add `"ENDCT2"` to disable this check) |

None. A missing `end` cannot be fixed automatically because the intended position of the `end` depends on the surrounding block structure.

This check triggers on the following tree-sitter node types:

- `ERROR` — a node whose text (or previous sibling) contains a block-opening keyword and which does not contain an `end`

- `ENDCT` — generic possible missing `end`
- `ENDCT3` — an END might be missing before a block-opening keyword
- `ENDCT4` — a METHODS block or END might be missing before a function definition

**Category:** Syntax Errors

- **Cascade**: A missing `methods` keyword confuses the parser, which can produce several additional spurious errors; fixing it removes the whole cascade

## Examples

### Correct

```matlab
classdef Foo
    methods
        function f()
            x = 1;
        end
    end
end
```

### Incorrect

```matlab
classdef Foo
    function f()    % ENDCT4 fires here

    end
end
